🚀 git-graffiti | Rust
🎯 Primary Use Case: To generate visually appealing or specific hexadecimal prefixes for Git commit hashes, enabling the creation of hex art or 'message-like' commit logs, despite the lack of practical utility.
✨ Key Features: • Brute-force commit hashes to achieve custom prefixes. • Rewrite Git history with modified commit hashes. • Append whitespace (spaces and tabs) as a nonce for hash manipulation.
📖 Summary: Git-graffiti is a Rust tool that allows users to manipulate Git commit hashes by brute-forcing the SHA-1 algorithm to create custom prefixes. It achieves this by appending whitespace characters as a nonce to commit messages and then rewriting history to display these custom hashes, enabling the creation of hex art or specific hash patterns in the commit log.

💡 oh-my-mermaid | TypeScript
🎯 Primary Use Case: To automatically generate and visualize software architecture documentation from codebases using AI, making complex systems easier to understand.
✨ Key Features: • AI-powered codebase analysis • Automatic generation of architecture diagrams (Mermaid.js) • Hierarchical and recursive analysis of code structure • Generation of documentation fields (description, context, etc.) • Interactive viewer for exploring diagrams
📖 Summary: Oh-my-mermaid (omm) is a command-line tool that leverages AI to automatically generate architecture diagrams and documentation from complex codebases. It helps developers visualize and understand their code's structure, data flow, and integrations, transforming code into human-readable architecture documentation.
🔗 Links: • View Project ================ 🔓 Open Source

✨ FolderOrganizer | JavaScript
🎯 Primary Use Case: Automating the organization of downloaded or miscellaneous files into predefined or custom-defined folder structures on Windows and Linux operating systems.
✨ Key Features: • Automatic file organization • Customizable rules • File classification by extension • Automatic execution via Windows Service or systemd service • Manual execution option
📖 Summary: FolderOrganizer is an open-source application for Windows and Linux that automates file organization. It monitors specified directories and moves files into categorized folders based on customizable rules, file extensions, and predefined structures.
🔗 Links: • View Project • Homepage ================ 🔓 Open Source

✨ quickemu | Shell
🎯 Primary Use Case: To quickly and easily create and run optimized virtual machines for various operating systems, including Windows and macOS, on Linux and macOS hosts.
✨ Key Features: • Automated OS downloads and VM configuration • Optimized VM settings based on host hardware • Support for Windows (including TPM 2.0), macOS, Linux, BSDs, and other OSs • ARM64 guest support • Full SPICE and VirtIO-webdavd/9p file sharing
📖 Summary: Quickemu is a shell script wrapper for QEMU that simplifies the creation and management of optimized virtual machines for Windows, macOS, and various Linux distributions. It automates the download of operating systems and configures VMs with optimal settings for the host hardware, requiring minimal user intervention.
🔗 Links: • View Project ================ 🔓 Open Source

🔥 fastapi-silk | Python
🎯 Primary Use Case: To provide developers with detailed insights into the performance of SQL queries within their FastAPI applications, helping to identify and optimize slow database operations.
✨ Key Features: • SQL instrumentation via SQLAlchemy engine events • Request-level metrics (X-DB-Queries, X-DB-Time, X-Total-Time headers) • Slow query logging to stdout • Per-request context isolation using contextvars • Minimal setup with one profiler call and middleware registration
📖 Summary: FastAPI-Silk is a lightweight middleware for FastAPI applications that profiles SQL queries executed through SQLAlchemy. It tracks query counts, database execution times, and total request times, providing this information via response headers and an interactive UI.
